full_judgment: 9. Md. Tazul Islam has referred a case reported in 4 MLR (AD) 1999 page 18 and referring to paragraph no.5 submitted that in a similar case their lordships of the Appellate Division found that the courts did not accept the transfer as an exchange but held the transaction is pre-emptible under the provision of Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and in this case the courts below having not held as such committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice. In the above decision their lordships held: "5. Mr. Miah Abdul Gafur, learned Advocate on Record for the petitioner submits that on the very face of the deed in question the transaction is an exchange. The courts below as well as the High Court Division committed an error of law in not holding that the transaction was not pre-emptible under the provisions of section 96 (10) (b) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950. Mr. Gafur's submission is not tenable in view of the concurrent finding of the courts below that the transaction is not an exchange but a sale, which has been rightly maintained by the High Court Division. Mr. Gafur next submits that the courts below did not consider that the pre-emptees made considerable improvement in the land in question spending Tk.1,00,000/-. The trial court on consideration of the evidence on record disbelieved the pre-emptees case of improvement which has also been affirmed by the lower appellate court."
